title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
The page finishes Lemma 2(b), the endpoint case. It then gives a Scholie and opens §3 'Recollement' (gluing), which leads into Th. 4 on the next page.

Setting. K is a finite union of topological arcs (a graph) in C, or in a Riemann surface, assumed somewhat regular (rectifiable or smooth). H is the closed upper half-plane and D° is the open unit disc.

Lemma 2(a), previous page. If x is not an endpoint of K, then for each side ('rive') of K at x there is a continuous map f : H∩D° → C. It is holomorphic and injective on (Int H)∩D°, sends ]-1,1[ into K with f(0)=x, and the chosen side is the one filled by f(Int H ∩ D°). This is a local boundary chart of the half-plane type.

Lemma 2(b), this page. If x is an endpoint of K, there is a continuous f : H∩D° → C, holomorphic in the interior, with three properties:
(a) f is injective on (Int H)∩D°, with image in C∖K;
(b) f(0)=x;
(c) f|]-1,0] and f|[0,1[ are each injective and have the same image in K.
So the boundary diameter is folded at 0 onto the arc ending at x. The model is z ↦ z² on the half-disc, mapping onto a disc slit along [0,1[. In words: near an endpoint, the slit neighbourhood is conformally a half-disc, and both sides of the slit are seen from the single half-disc.

Scholie. Each side of K gives K (away from vertices) a canonical real-analytic structure. Take local charts f as in the lemma. The boundary values of f identify open pieces of K with intervals of R. Two such charts on the same side differ by a conformal map between half-discs. By Schwarz reflection that map is real-analytic on the real segment, so the structure is canonical, and intrinsic to the embedding of K in any Riemann surface.

The two sides, however, give different structures. The identity of K, read through the two sides' charts, is a homeomorphism that is in general not real-analytic. Grothendieck adds that C^∞ or analytic regularity of these side-structures does not reflect the regularity of K as a subset of C. In modern terms, the comparison map between the two sides is exactly the conformal welding homeomorphism of K. A fuller Scholie is promised after the next theorem.

§3 Recollement. This announces Th. 4 (next page), an equivalence of categories between:
- triples (X, K, S): X a compact bordered Riemann surface, (K,S) a compact topological graph (S its vertices) with ∂X ⊂ K ⊂ X;
- triples (X̃, S̃, σ): X̃ a compact bordered Riemann surface, S̃ a finite subset of ∂X̃, σ an involution of the cut-open boundary ∂X̃ cut at S̃, satisfying some regularity.
The functor X ↦ X̃ cuts X open along K, using Th. 3 and the side-charts of Lemma 2. The inverse glues X̃ by σ. On X = X̃/R one takes as structure sheaf the continuous functions that are holomorphic off K. The whole is a categorical, graph-based form of conformal cutting and welding. It serves the 'surgery' of conformal surfaces, e.g. building Riemann surfaces from polygons or triangles glued along edges (cf. dessins / Esquisse, 1984).
errors: The canonicity claim in the Scholie is correct (Carathéodory extension plus Schwarz reflection), but only at non-vertex points. At vertices of order ≥2 and at endpoints, the structure is singular: at an endpoint, the arc is parametrized by t ↦ f(±√t)-type charts.
The planned Th. 4 is not correct as an equivalence with a naive regularity condition on σ such as 'rectifiable par morceaux', which is not even a meaningful condition on a homeomorphism.

Direction a)→b): rectifiable (σ-finite length) arcs are removable for continuous functions holomorphic off them (Besicovitch/Painlevé type), so the cut-and-reglue structure is recovered. That direction is fine.

Direction b)→a): for an arbitrary homeomorphism σ, the sheaf of continuous functions holomorphic off K need not define a Riemann surface structure, and gluings need not exist or be unique. This is the conformal welding problem: existence and uniqueness hold e.g. for quasisymmetric σ, and fail in general (non-removable curves, non-unique weldings).

The welding homeomorphisms coming from rectifiable K are not characterized by any simple regularity class. So the essential image of a)→b) is not described by the stated condition; one would need e.g. 'σ quasisymmetric', with K then quasi-arcs.
Minor: 'f|(I×H)∩D°' in condition (a) must be (Int H)∩D°.

ideas.what: Local uniformization of the complement of an arc near an interior point (half-disc chart for each side) and near an endpoint (folding chart, z ↦ z² model)
ideas.modern_name: Boundary correspondence / Carathéodory extension for slit domains; prime ends at arc endpoints

ideas.what: Each side of an arc in a Riemann surface induces a canonical real-analytic structure on the arc; the two structures differ by a non-analytic homeomorphism that need not reflect the regularity of the arc
ideas.modern_name: Conformal welding homeomorphism of a curve (two-sided boundary correspondence)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pfluger (1960), Lehto–Virtanen (1960); Kikuchi; later Bishop, Sheffield

ideas.what: Equivalence of categories between (bordered surface, embedded graph containing boundary) and (cut-open bordered surface, finite boundary set, boundary involution), with the conformal structure on the glued surface defined by continuous functions holomorphic off K
ideas.modern_name: Conformal welding / sewing of Riemann surfaces along graphs (ribbon-graph gluing)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Welding: Pfluger, Lehto–Virtanen; graph/tree weldings: Bishop ('true trees'), Marshall–Rohde; gluing of polygons: classical (Riemann/Schwarz)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses building Riemann surfaces from combinatorial maps by gluing, but not this welding formalism

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates the two-sided boundary structures of an embedded graph, and the non-analytic identification between them (the welding map), as the key regularity datum for 'surgery' of conformal surfaces. This links the dessins/gluing programme to conformal welding. The welding viewpoint on dessins (Bishop's true trees, conformal welding of trees) appeared only ~30 years later.
missed.quote: Chaque rive de K munit K d'une structure analytique réelle canonique ... mais le passage de l'une à l'autre se fait par une application (identique) qui n'est pas une iso analytique
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor of the welding approach to dessins d'enfants and to gluing Riemann surfaces along graphs. It is not new mathematics; the welding facts were known to analysts since 1960.

missed.claim: A promised 'Scholie plus circonstancié' on the regularity of the gluing function was to make the regularity hypothesis on σ in Th. 4 precise. As written, the hypothesis is inadequate: the right condition is quasisymmetry or a removability hypothesis.
missed.quote: ceci devrait se magnifier dans un Scholie plus circonstancié au théorème suivant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. The correct theory (quasisymmetric welding, removability) already exists in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is classical: Carathéodory boundary correspondence and conformal welding (Pfluger, Lehto–Virtanen 1960). Grothendieck rediscovers welding in a categorical, graph-based form for his surgery/dessins programme, and the regularity claim of the planned equivalence is too naive. Historically mildly interesting as a welding-based precursor to later work on dessins, but not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Condition a): 'f|(I × H) ∩ D°' should read 'f|(Int H) ∩ D°'.
The crossed-out word before 'munit' is likely 'est muni' (originally 'Chaque rive de K est munie...' corrected to 'munit K d'une').
'(ceci devrait se magnifier dans un Scholie plus circonstancié au théorème suivant)' — 'devrait' is inserted above the line, and 'se' is not struck in the image.
The parenthetical reads approximately '(fonction C^∞, ou analytique réel etc)', with 'fonction' crossed out or abbreviated.
'reflètent pas toutes...' is probably 'ne reflètent pas toutes les propriétés de régularité correspondantes de K dans C'.
